name: Tarun Ramprakash
headline: Aerospace researcher — CFD and solver development
summaryShort: I build the solvers that make transonic aerodynamics computable — and study where they stop being trustworthy.
summaryLong: I work on computational fluid dynamics from the inside: writing the solvers rather than only running them. My MSc research at Cranfield rebuilt a viscous full-potential method for transonic aircraft design, and the more interesting half of that work was not making it converge — it was finding the precise physical conditions under which it cannot.

That question runs through most of what I do. A low-fidelity method is useful exactly as far as its assumptions hold, and knowing where the edge is matters more than another decimal place inside it. I spend my time on gradient reconstruction schemes, shock-induced boundary-layer separation, parallel finite-volume solvers in C++/MPI, and increasingly on where machine learning genuinely helps rather than merely fits.

Before the solvers I designed the aircraft. I led the aerodynamic and structural work on a UAV concept that carried a 30 kg payload to 19,024 ft, which is a useful grounding: it is harder to be careless about a model when you have watched the thing it describes fly.
availability: Open to collaboration — academic or industrial
